deep.reconstruction:
There is no mathematics on this page. It is a financial memorandum: a list of bond (Obligation) numbers drawn by lot for redemption ('Zurück' = called back / repaid) at four quarterly dates. It continues the list on folio 59, which covers 1 Jul 1850 to 1 Apr 1851. Each draw lists numbers by series A–E.

Draws on this page:
(1) 'Zurück 1/7 1851' (1 July 1851): A 197, 392; B 605, 703, 815, 1054; C 1600, 1603, 1692, 2089; D 2283, 2430, 2664, 2685, 2769; E 3461, 3693, 3724, 3849.
(2) 1/10 1851: A 59, 132; B 513, 1027, 1120, 1221, 1239; C 1550, 1581, 1881, 2047; D 2179, 2290, 2439, 2610, 2703; E 3342, 3521, 3617, 3749.
(3) 1/1 1852: A 343, 377; B 518, 519, 740, 1072, 1197; C 1312, 1356, 1601, 2012; D 2196, 2219, 2232, 2824, 2853; E 3157, 3259, 3400, 3696.
(4) 1/4 1852: A 118, 367; B 670, 718, 1020, 1117, 1170; C 1379, 1481, 1598, 1784; D 2560, 2578, 2688, 2780, 2792; E 3347, 3629, 3742, 3855.

The series occupy consecutive number ranges, judging from this page and folio 59: A roughly 1–500, B 500–1300, C 1300–2100, D 2100–3100, E 3100–3900. That suggests one loan of about 3900 bonds.

The number drawn per quarter is A:2, B:4–5, C:4, D:5, E:4, giving 19 or 20 per draw. On folio 59 Gauss wrote these counts explicitly as '2A 4B 4C 5D 4E'. The counts are roughly proportional to the size of each series, about 1 bond in 200 per quarter, or about 2% amortization per year. This interpretation (proportional quotas, possibly series = denominations) is mine and is not stated by Gauss.

The next page (61) starts a separate list ('Ausgeloosete Wexiö', half-yearly draws on 1/6 and 1/12). That appears to be a different loan, presumably connected with Växjö, Sweden; this is a reading of the next page's heading, not something confirmed here.

Purpose: Gauss was keeping track of whether bonds he held, or was monitoring (for example for the Göttingen widows' fund or his own investments), had been drawn for repayment.
errors: No computational errors are possible; it is a record of lottery numbers. Within each series and draw the numbers are in strictly increasing order, consistent with careful copying from a published drawing list.

There are corrections in the manuscript. E 3724 (1/7 1851) has a 4 written over another digit. D 2824 (1/1 1852) has a corrected final 4. D 2560 (1/4 1852) has the 6 written over another digit, possibly 2510 corrected to 2560. These look like Gauss correcting his own copying slips.

results.what: Record of bonds drawn for redemption from a serially numbered loan (series A–E, about 3900 numbers) at quarterly drawings from July 1851 to April 1852
results.modern_name: Sinking-fund / amortization lottery drawing of bond numbers (personal financial bookkeeping)

deep.surprise_reason: This is purely a bookkeeping list of drawn bond numbers. It contains no mathematics. Gauss's careful financial affairs and bond investments are well documented.

checkable.asserts: Every series list in every draw is strictly increasing, as copied from an official drawing list.
No bond number is drawn twice across the four draws; there are 19+20+20+20 = 79 distinct numbers.
Number of bonds redeemed per quarterly draw.

transcription_corrections: E line of 1/7 1851: '3724' is correct, but the final 4 is written over another digit (overwrite rather than an uncertain reading).
D line of 1/1 1852: '2824' has a corrected/overwritten final 4.
D line of 1/4 1852: '2560' has the 6 written over another digit (possibly 2510 corrected to 2560); 2560 is the final intended reading.
The heading of the last draw reads 'Zurück 1/4 1852'; the numerator 1 is written as a heavy dot-like stroke.
